name: Symfony Mailer office365
description: Adds an Office 365 / Microsoft 365 OAuth2 (XOAUTH2) SMTP transport to Symfony Mailer, replacing retired basic-auth SMTP.
provides_drush_commands: symfony_mailer_office365:refresh (alias office365:refresh) — refresh the stored OAuth access token if expired; --force refreshes unconditionally
provides_plugin_types: Provides an Office 365 transport for Symfony Mailer: a Symfony Mailer transport-factory service (Office365EsmtpTransportFactory, tag mailer.transport_factory, schemes office365/microsoft) plus a symfony_mailer MailerTransport plugin instance office365_oauth (Office 365 - OAuth). It does not define a new plugin type.
project_description: Symfony Mailer Office365 Integration. Office 365 has been retiring support for sending mail via SMTP with basic authentication (username and password), which requires a modern OAuth 2.0 flow. This module fills that gap for the symfony_mailer (Symfony Mailer) module: it authenticates to smtp.office365.com over SMTP using the XOAUTH2 SASL mechanism with an OAuth2 access token, obtained through the delegated authorization-code flow against login.microsoftonline.com and stored in Drupal state. Setup: register an app in Microsoft Entra with redirect URL /office365/oauth/callback, enter Client ID, Client Secret, Tenant ID and the sending e-mail at /admin/config/system/mailer/office365, add the 'Office 365 - OAuth' transport to a Symfony Mailer mailing policy, then click 'Login via Microsoft' to complete interactive consent and store the token. The refresh token keeps the access token alive: refreshing happens on Drupal cron (run at least every 12 hours) or via 'drush office365:refresh'. Client credentials may also be overridden from settings.local.php via $config['symfony_mailer_office365.config']. Inspired by community gists; may become obsolete once Symfony ships native support.
